current_focus.domain: Product media: image, gallery, placeholder, sizes and alt text referencing EmDash's Media Library (WooCommerce model)
current_focus.summary: Maintainer chose option C and the Lingui lever (2026-10-07). Outcome: a clerk opens a product in the installed sandbox admin, chooses an image and gallery images from the Commerce-rendered Media Library page (media:read), reorders and removes gallery images, and chooses a store placeholder in Commerce Settings; GET catalog/public returns image and gallery as { id, alt, width, height, placeholder } with alt read live (alt, caption, product name); the disposable server-rendered storefront fixture resolves ids to public file URLs through the EmDash host and renders srcset through EmDash's image endpoint with Commerce preset constants; a product without an image returns the placeholder with placeholder: true, or image: null when none is set. Implementation: id-only catalog_media and storefront_placeholder_image records, media:read capability, Block Kit Images/Gallery/Placeholder sections and library chooser, native save-media and placeholder-image routes, exported preset constants and URL helpers, oslojs side-effect-free marking and the Lingui runtime swap with an equivalence test; recorded size and hash. Proof: unit tests, public-catalog test, Playwright sandbox run with screenshots, packaging equivalence and browser suites. Excluded: imports, CDN offload, regeneration, video, variants, native React chooser, publication, merge.

alternatives: Variations: sellable variants with a per-variation image that falls back to the parent product image, then to the store placeholder (rule recorded in product-media-reference-001), together with variant price and SKU identity.

Host picker and URL parity: when Block Kit renders media_picker on plugin admin pages and the plugin media item carries a public URL or storage key, replace the Commerce-rendered chooser with the host element and let the public catalog carry src/srcset directly; includes batching or bounded caching of per-request media reads.
recommendation.reason: Decision 7 deferred imports and extensions to a media plugin by design; it is the next WooCommerce-shaped gap now that product references, live alt and the placeholder exist. Variations are the next catalog gap the recorded fallback rule already anticipates. The host-parity alternative depends on EmDash changes outside this repository.
recommendation.recommended: Media plugin as WooCommerce's extension layer: bulk and feed import deduped by recorded source URL and content hash, CDN offload, size regeneration and video galleries, implemented as a separate plugin that talks to EmDash's media API (media:write / media:bytes:read) and to Commerce's product references (catalog-items/save-media), never to a store of its own; first grill settles the import contract and the dedupe keys.

pause.next_safe_action: After the maintainer merges or returns the pull request, resume with the recommended media-plugin grill (or an alternative) on a fresh branch from main; do not merge, publish or deploy from this track.
pause.reason: Slice delivered to pull request dinkuskit/commerce#57 (head f964a3d, review-clean source 5cb59c6c302b8255e5c23b55fca8f31d28037361). Maintainer gates remain: pull request review and ClawSweeper trigger, merge, any Registry publication (media:read is a declared-access change), and the decision-5 wording amendment about the host resolution path.

decisions.choice: A product references EmDash Media Library items by media id only; Commerce stores no file, URL, alt or size copy. One isolated record per product (catalog_media sandbox / catalogMedia native, recordKind catalog-media, recordId = catalogItemId) holds image (one media id or null) and gallery (an ordered list of media ids, max 8, no duplicates). EmDash 1.2.0 exposes no plugin-visible mapping between a media id and the public file URL, so the public URL is resolved by the storefront host and never stored. Products stay catalog records, not an EmDash content collection, so Commerce mirrors the reference shape instead of using the image field type. No darkVariant this slice. Variation rule recorded for later variant work: a variation image falls back to the parent product image, then to the store placeholder; Commerce has no variations yet (kind simple-product), so this slice implements product and placeholder only.

decisions.choice: Live at projection time through the EmDash plugin media access (ctx.media.get(mediaId)), declared as the media:read capability in emdash-plugin.jsonc and in native createPlugin. Alt resolves media alt, then media caption, then the product name, never the filename. A reference whose media item is missing, not ready or not an image is skipped in the gallery and replaced by the placeholder rule for the primary image; it never breaks the catalog. No alt or dimension copy is stored in Commerce. media:read is the only new grant; media:bytes:read, media:write and media:metadata:write stay undeclared.

decisions.choice: A Commerce setting: Commerce Settings -> Catalog -> Placeholder image, stored as an isolated storefront_placeholder_image (sandbox) / storefrontPlaceholderImage (native) record holding one media id or null; not an EmDash site setting, and Commerce ships no placeholder file. The public catalog returns the placeholder as image with placeholder: true when a product has no resolvable primary image; with no placeholder configured, image is null and the storefront decides. The placeholder never appears inside gallery.

decisions.choice: Two measured, behavior-preserving levers in the sandbox build: (1) mark pure @oslojs/* modules side-effect-free in the Rolldown input so unused auth passkey/OAuth crypto is dropped (about 5.6 KB); (2) replace the @lingui/core runtime in couponText with a local interpolator over the pinned compiled catalog, which scripts/coupon-catalog.mjs already restricts to plain strings and single-name placeholders (about 4.8 KB), guarded by a unit test proving equality with Lingui for every catalog message and edge values. No change to the audited auth transform, minify settings or coupon catalog contents. The proof records the new backend size and SHA-256 and reruns the coupon packaging equivalence test and every sandbox browser suite; the slice pauses rather than weakening a guard if the cap is still exceeded.

decisions.choice: The public catalog carries image and gallery[] entries as { id, alt, width, height, placeholder } resolved live from the Media Library (alt chain: media alt, caption, product name). Public URLs, srcset, sizes and thumbnails are produced by the storefront host, which can map a media id to its public file URL (Astro.locals.emdash.handleMediaGet or EmDash's Image component), using Commerce-named preset widths exported as constants (thumbnail 300, single 600, gallery_thumbnail 100; srcset candidates 300, 600, 1200 capped at the original width, sizes for the single width) and the exported commerceImageTransformUrl and commerceImageSrcset helpers over EmDash's image endpoint (/_image?href=<public file URL>&w=<width>&f=webp). No pre-generated files and no Commerce-served bytes; configurable presets and cropping are later grills.
decisions.domain: Product media: image, gallery, placeholder, sizes and alt text referencing EmDash's Media Library (WooCommerce model)

history.choice: Three Commerce-named presets as constants this slice (no settings UI): thumbnail 300px wide, single 600px wide, gallery_thumbnail 100px wide, width-only (no crop). Sizes are produced on demand by EmDash's image endpoint (/_image?href=<absolute src>&w=<width>&f=webp), never pre-generated files. Public catalog image and gallery[] entries carry { id, src, alt, width, height, srcset, sizes, thumbnail }: src is the original library file URL, srcset lists the single candidates (300, 600, 1200) capped at the original width, sizes targets the single width, thumbnail is the thumbnail preset URL for image and the gallery_thumbnail preset URL for gallery entries. A site that moves image.endpoint.route breaks srcset and thumbnail but never src; configurable presets, cropping and regeneration are later grills.
